## Summary

This PR updates the `/questions` and `/comments` endpoints to allow us to enable requiring start and end date on those endpoints.

## How to Test

### Basic state
1. Ensure the comments endpoint is enabled [local link](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_IsCommentContentFeedEndpointEnabled)
2. Ensure the new setting is turned off [local link](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled)
3. Make a request without start and end dates to the [questions endpoint](https://api.stackexchange.local/v3/sites/meta.stackexchange.local/questions)
4. Validate that you receive a 200 response
5. Repeat steps 3-4 for the [comments endpoint](https://api.stackexchange.local/v3/sites/meta.stackexchange.local/content-feeds/comments)
6. Make a call to a deep page of the [comments endpoint](https://api.stackexchange.local/v3/sites/meta.stackexchange.local/content-feeds/comments?page=1000) 
7. Validate that you do not get an error message about exceeding maximum items allowed

### With Site Setting
1. Turn the new setting on [local link](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled)
2. Set the [questions time range site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxDayRangeWindowForQuestions) 
3. Set the [comments time range site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxDayRangeWindowForComments) to a different value than the questions site setting
4. Make a request to the questions endpoint without a `to` parameter
5. Validate that you receive a bad request error
6. Repeat Steps 4-5 with the `from` parameter
7. Make a request with a date range that is larger than the window created in Step 2
8. Validate that you receive a bad request error
9. Make a request that is within the range from Step 2
10. Validate that you receive a 200 response
11. Make a request to the comments endpoint without a `creationto` parameter
12.  Validate that you receive a bad request error
13.  Repeat Steps 11-12 with the `creationfrom` parameter
14.  Make a request with a date range that is larger than the window created in Step 3
15. Validate that you receive a bad request error
16.  Make a request that is within the range from Step 3
17.  Validate that you receive a 200 response



---------------------------------------------------

author: SteffiPeTaffy
body:
## Summary  
This PR introduces a **comment spam risk heuristic** that evaluates whether a user is likely engaging in spammy behavior based on their flagged comments in the last 7 days. The score is computed and logged, but not yet used for enforcement.  

## Details  

### New Method  
- **`CalculateCommentSpamRiskScoreAsync(long? userId)`**  
  - Computes a 0–100 score for spam risk based on user’s comments and associated spam flags.  
  - Hopefully performant enough with a **single SQL query** fetching aggregates on every comment submit
  - Currently uses `Flags.FlagTypeId IN (20,45)` (spam/offensive) to identify risky comments.  

### Scoring Logic  
- **Ratio Score (0–60):**  
  - Proportion of flagged comments vs. total comments.  
  - Tiers:  
    - ≥ 75% flagged → +60  
    - ≥ 50% flagged → +40  
    - ≥ 25% flagged → +20  
    - else → 0  

- **Volume Score (0–40):**  
  - +10 points per flagged comment, capped at 40.  

- **Small Sample Dampening:**  
  - If user has fewer than 3 comments in the 7-day window, score is scaled down proportionally.  
  - Prevents users from being misclassified as high-risk based on a single flagged comment.  

### Behavior  
- Returns **0** if:  
  - `userId` is null, or  
  - user has **no comments** in the past 7 days.  
- Final score is **clamped between 0–100**.  
- At this stage, the score is only **logged in AEH events** for evaluation, not yet tied to moderation actions.  

### Performance & Design Note  
- It’s **not ideal** to query the database on every comment submit.  
- However, until we build a **dedicated trustworthiness domain/service**, this is a pragmatic and **performant enough compromise** (single aggregate query, limited to 7 days of data).  
- This allows us to start evaluating the usefulness of the score immediately while planning a more scalable design later.  

## Why This Matters  
- Helps detect **human spammers** who post many comments that quickly get flagged.  
- Complements the **Dormant-Burst Score** (focused on sleeper accounts).  
- Adds another signal we can use in evaluating **trustworthiness and spam risk**.  

## Next Steps  
- Evaluate logged data and calibrate thresholds.  
- Consider integrating with automated restrictions (e.g., temporary comment cooldowns).  
- Extend heuristic to include **comment deletion patterns** if needed.
title: Add Comment Spam Risk Score

author: SteffiPeTaffy
body:
# PR: Add dormant-burst risk score for users

## Motivation
We’ve seen in the past that *pre-registered sleeper accounts* can suddenly reactivate and start spamming (human bot farms).  
To help detect these patterns early, we’re introducing a **dormant-burst heuristic** that scores accounts based on their age, inactivity, and visit history.  
This score can be used to gate comment creation, throttle risky users, or flag suspicious accounts for moderation.

## What’s new
- **Introduced `UserScoreService`** implementing `IUserScoreService`.
- Added `CalculateDormantBurstScore(ICurrentUser)` method:
  - Returns a **risk score (0–100)** where higher = more suspicious.
  - Based on three simple, explainable signals:
    - **Account age**
      - +30 if account is **old** (≥ 90 days).
    - **Inactivity gap**
      - +30 if **last access ≥ 60 days ago** or user has **never accessed**.
    - **Visit history**
      - +40 if ≤ 1 total day visited.
      - +20 if ≤ 5 days visited.
      - +0 if ≤ 20 days visited.
      - −20 if > 20 days visited (lowers risk for steady users).
- Score is **clamped between 0 and 100**.

## Example outcomes
- **New, active users** → score ~0.
- **Older, sporadic users** → score in the 20–50 range.
- **Dormant sleeper accounts** (old + long inactive + never visited) → score up to 100.

## Why this matters
- Provides a **transparent and tunable** way to assess trustworthiness.
- Helps distinguish between:
  - Legitimate new users experimenting with comments.
  - Low-effort spammers.
  - Potential bot farm accounts waking up after long dormancy.
- This is a **first step** in building a broader trust / spam-resistance framework for comments.

## Next steps
- Integrate this score into comment throttling / mod review pipeline.
- Combine with other heuristics (reputation, penalty history, content checks).
- Calibrate thresholds after observing real traffic.
title: First skeleton for user scores

body: PubPlat's and SOE's CNAB invocation images, are pretty stable, after all they implement deployment pipelines which should be fairly stable. With this in mind, I thought this would be a good candidate to start trying out Docker layer caching and avoid rebuilding every layer if nothing really changed. This is using Github's cache, which is pretty restrictive (10GB max). The result is that in Enterprise, the CNAB image build step drops from 3 minutes, to 15-60 secs: In Public and Teams, as Pubplat's CNAB image is build in parallel as part of the same docker bake that the app images are built, the impact on the runtime is not noticeable, however in the logs it can be seen that it was cached: As part of the test, I tried caching the `nuget-cache` step, which does all the restores, and although it works it takes a lot of space in the cache and we are constantly getting over the 10GBs, evicting thing and making the whole cache unstable (lots of unexpected misses). There is an alternative, where you can cache the layers to a registry. I haven't tried it, but it seems that it builds a cache image and uses the registry as the cache storage. Given the cost issues that we have with Cloudsmith, I don't think using them would be a good idea, but wonder if maybe using another registry (Azure or GCP) to store caches could work.

Slack context: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/CNAE3JWEP/p1754605298090239

This PR decouples `RedirectVoteActionHandler` from the DI system and removes the service locator pattern around it so that code testing post votes (e.g. in #23587) doesn't need to set up a whole DI service provider and register a mock instance of this class on `BaseTest`.

This PR keeps `RedirectVoteActionHandler` unit-testable for verifying its functionality works with various handlers, while also letting production code just use an instance of that class that uses the default handlers that you need in production. 

If tests need to exercise some post voting functionality but want to inject their own specific `RedirectVoteActionHandler` to use, then that dependency can be added as parameters more locally to the code instead (in a followup PR). In practical terms that means if say you're testing `Posts2Vote.EnsureVotingRightsAsync` and want a custom `RedirectVoteActionHandler`, you can add a parameter to `Posts2Vote.EnsureVotingRightsAsync` to take that in, and by default callers can use `RedirectVoteActionHandler.Default`.

Making these changes I hope will make it so that "how do I handle a failed post vote" is less of a global app concern (registered globally at startup) and more of a specific concern to the post voting code itself.
title: Decouple RedirectVoteActionHandler from DI

**Note:** No test because the behaviour is only surfaced when running for reals unfortunately and it's impossible to simulate the error in a unit test 🤷 

This PR solves the problem where calls through the Fragment Proxy that yield a response that should not have content throw an `InvalidOperationException` when attempting to copy empty content.

The full exception is like this:

```
System.InvalidOperationException: Writing to the response body is invalid for responses with status code 204.
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.Internal.Http.HttpProtocol.FirstWriteAsyncInternal(ReadOnlyMemory`1 data, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.Internal.Http.HttpProtocol.WritePipeAsync(ReadOnlyMemory`1 data, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.ResponseCompression.ResponseCompressionBody.WriteAsync(ReadOnlyMemory`1 buffer, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
   at System.Net.Http.HttpContent.<CopyToAsync>g__WaitAsync|56_0(ValueTask copyTask)
   at StackOverflow.FragmentProxy.HtmlFragmentProxy.WriteToContextResponseAsync(HttpContext context, HttpResponseMessage response, CancellationToken cancellationToken) in /app/src/StackOverflow.Common.AspNet/FragmentProxy/HtmlFragmentProxy.cs:line 275
   at StackOverflow.FragmentProxy.HtmlFragmentProxy.ProxyRequestAsync(HttpContext httpContext, String xsrfFormValue, String requestIpAddress, Nullable`1 userId, String sitePrefix, String jwt, CancellationToken cancellationToken) in /app/src/StackOverflow.Common.AspNet/FragmentProxy/HtmlFragmentProxy.cs:line 140
```

To handle this scenario this PR will not attempt to copy a response in these situations:

- HTTP status code is 1xx
- HTTP status code is 204, 205 or 304
- response `Content-Length` is zero
title: [FRAGMENT PROXY] No content responses

author: balpha
body:
I created the controller builder so that there's a typesafe, single-source-of-truth way to create Stimulus controllers without error-prone `declare`s and copy&pastes, which is the Stimulus-recommended way of doing things when working with TypeScript.

I was looking around at the many uses of the controller builder in our codebase, and I noticed that the single most often encountered shortfall of the typings is the fact that targets are always typed as `HTMLElement`, so people often had to resort to type assertions like

```ts
(this.myButtonTarget as HTMLButtonElement).disabled = false;
```

This changeset makes it possible to (optionally) specify the element type at definition time, like this:

```ts
.withTargets("myButton")<HTMLButtonElement>()
```

Yes, I agree that this syntax looks slightly weird, and I've debated many different approaches before I settled on this. I think it's intuitively clear from reading it what's happening.

The most obvious solution would have been this:

```ts
.withTargets<HTMLButtonElement>("myButton")
```

but unfortunately this doesn't work, because Typescript does not allow partial type argument inference, and `withTargets` needs to infer the target name types. I didn't want to force the user to duplicate them with something like

```ts
.withTargets<HTMLFormElement, "myForm" | "myOtherForm">("myForm", "myOtherForm")
```

because that is much less readable.

I also considered (and actually originally implemented) a method called `ofTargetElementType` that you could directly chain behind a `withTargets` call. This is very similar to the solution I ultimately went with, but it has the disadvantage that Prettier will move it to the next line:

```ts
... = buildController("something-or-other")
    .withTargets("foo")
    .ofTargetElementType<HTMLCanvasElement>()
    .withClasses("bar")
    ...
```

and that makes it much less obvious to the reader of the code that the two belong tightly together.

Finally, this would also have been possible:

```ts
.withTargets<HTMLButtonElement>()("myButton")
```

but this doesn't feel any more elegant than my chosen solution, and it has the disadvantage that you would either need two different functions (`.withTargets` and `.withTargetsOfType`), or add additional complexity from added overload behavior of `withTargets()`.

That's why I went with what I went with.

I also added a couple of unit tests to verify the runtime behavior of the controller builder. There has always been an extensive "test suite" of the *typings*, and they are clearly the more complex piece of the puzzle. But especially with the added complexity of `.withTargets()`, including additions to the runtime behavior, I felt I should also add some validation that the builder actually builds controller classes as expected.
title: controller builder: allow narrowing the element types of targets

body:
With the recent work that Scale did, we isolated the first main site’s database alongside the Sites and ChannelsDB. However, the PublicTest network (or any other used by the integration tests) has more sites than that. For example, Literaturature, Meta Literature, StackApps, etc. 

Some tests switch to these sites with methods defined in `BaseTest`, such as `WithMainSite` or `WithLiteratureSite`. The problem is that when for example the current database is Literature, and the test is using the `IsolatedDatabaseTest` base class, it runs on an isolated SitesDB but in a non isolated ContentDB. 

This PR fixes that by:
- During bootstrapping it takes a backup of all the content database of each site in the testing network (i.e. PublicTest)
- The `IsolatedDatabaseTest` keeps restoring the SitesDB and the network's principal's site content DB (the default used by every test). 
- `IsolatedDatabaseTest` overrides the `With{Site}` methods, by creating an isolated version of that site's content DB and overriding **again** the connectionstring mappings. So now when the test switches to a new site, that site's DB is also isolated and the test hit that DB. We only restore it once per TestClass, same concept as with the principal's site content DB and SitesDB. 

This is how a test that uses `WithMainSite` looked like before. You can see in the items watched at the bottom, that the originalCurrentDB and sitesDB point to an isolated test (have a guid at the end), while the currentDB doesnt:

author: ProductiveRage
body:
## The history
In PR #22971, I had changed a line in the `static StagingGroundPrefs Get(int userId)` method following this call:

```
var json = cn.DB.QuerySingleOrDefault<string>("Select StagingGroundPrefs From UserMetadata Where UserId = @Id", new { Id = userId });
```

When I was writing unit tests for the `QuestionsController`, `cn.DB.QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` was returning null and I presumed that it must have been a behaviour of `QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` that I had misunderstood, and that its concept of `null` for a `string` was a default blank string value. As such, I changed the `??` null coalesce check into `string.IsNullOrEmpty(..)` and my test code worked, and all other tests did, and I went about my day.

In that PR, there was [a comment](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/22971#discussion_r2131851337) from @gcasar  -

> This bit I do feel strongly about - its tackling a totally unrelated bug to the code and I'd like us to move it to a separate PR in the future. That way its easier to revert/review on its own.

## The confusion
Although it didn't block that PR, it weighed on me, and I dug into it again.

It turns out that an `NSubstitute`-instantiated `IDBContext` reference will return a blank value (rather than `null`) from any method that returns a `string` that hasn't had a behaviour explicitly specified. So it was only _my test code_ that was affected.

## The controversy
I could have specified a behaviour on the `NSubstitute`-provided `IDBContext`, such `QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` calls would return null (overriding the `NSubstitute` blank-string default). And maybe I should have done! (This PR is a draft, and a discussion, and so I may backtrack, if you think that what I did instead is terrible).

Overriding `IDBContext` methods is such a coarse way of mocking things out in our unit tests, and so it always gets my shackles up. Plus, I felt like this was a really weird, surprising decision on the part of `NSubstitute` (is everyone else aware of it??)

As such, I did some Googling, and found a way to add some code (by reading [GitHub issues, like this one](https://github.com/nsubstitute/NSubstitute/pull/705#issuecomment-1285460860) to the `StackOverflowUnitTestFramework`* so that every test that uses that class will get `null` strings by default from `string`-returning methods of mocks that have not had explicit behaviour assigned.

\* _(Currently, the projects `StackOverflow.Tests.Unit` and `StackOverflow.Tests.Unit.Common` and `StackOverflow.Tests.Unit.RazorViews` all use `StackOverflowUnitTestFramework` but there are unit test projects for modules that do not - I have avoided meddling with them too much, though it may be worth thinking about in the near future; how consistent they should be with our "main" unit test projects)_

## The ask
I could genuinely go either way on this. If a review strongly suggests that I change the code that changes the `NSubstitute` default behaviour (particularly if you, or others, find it logical and/or non-surprising) then I'll remove the "magic" and stub out the `cn.DB.QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` in my test code.

But I wanted to get an opinion about whether this was going to _reduce_ confusion in the future.

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
The Fragment Proxy allows you to register a service prefix such as `/my-service` in the monolith for which all requests will be proxied to another service to provide UI pages and components inside the monolith.

However, the registration of service prefixes happens after the monolith routes have been registered which means that if there is a service prefix that overlaps with an existing route, the existing route will not be handled.

For example:

- Given the monolith route `/feature-x/list`
- Given the service prefix `/feature-x` in `fragment-proxies.*.json`

Calling `https://stackoverflow.com/feature-x/list` is now proxied to the service rather than being handled by the monolith.

As the Fragment Proxy also registers a wild card route there is no straightforward way to decide which one should "win".
Therefore, this PR introduces a check that when service prefixes are registered it will look for overlaps and refuse to start the application.

The error is logged and looks like this:

```
System.InvalidOperationException: The service prefix for Fragment Proxy must be unique.
Found conflicting routes for service prefix: /feature-x:
- feature-x/list
```
title: [FRAGMENT PROXY] Refuse to start if a service prefix overlaps

author: ProductiveRage
body:
… there may be ONE outlier that needs something different, and then you have to undo things for that one test because you tied yourself to a constructor that has code that "surely will apply in _all_ possible cases".

The changes here have ended up being an illustration of how we _could_ do it, rather than being an illustration of where we could immediately _benefit from doing so_.

I made the changes when I was looking at isolating Elastic from the test `UsersCanViewPublicDiscussionList` in `CollectivePublicDiscussionsControllerTests` and imagined that I would mock out Elastic by mocking out `ICollectiveDiscussionsService` (and so I would a different implementation of that interface in this one particular test).

However, the `CollectiveDiscussionsService` implementation of that interface does _a lot_, and mocking out all of it just to isolate Elastic made me feel like the test wouldn't actually be testing much any more! (Which suggests an opportunity to improve the design.. but it's not been a priority).

## What are you trying to do here??
We _can_ structure our code to remove duplication, without shoving it into constructors, which results in test setup code being spread around rather than being nicely localised.

Sadly, it's a pattern that I've seen happen at Stack quite often ("oh, should we throw that repeated code into the constructor") but the benefits don't offset the costs, in my experience. So if we can demonstrate a way to get the best of both worlds (cut down on duplicated code, have localised arrange / act / assert test code, _and_ make it easy for some tests to use a different configuration) then we might be able to slowly turn the tide.

author: ProductiveRage
body:
Reverts #22763 - as discussed on a call on Friday with Scale Pod, I think that there could be some useful learnings in here for when we start leaning more heavily into unit tests (where "unit test" means no shared state, no out-of-process comms - rather than it meaning "a single unit of code under test") but I also understand that it means that where we used to have test coverage that exercised our Redis integration (even if that isn't explicitly part of the test's intent) we would no longer have that.

I think that we should aim to have fewer tests rely on dependencies that they don't really care about (like Redis, in the case of many tests) but that should be done in tandem with adding some tests that _do_ explicitly test the functionality the relies upon Redis. While the PR being reverted demonstrated how that could be done, it didn't look for everywhere that it _should_ be done, and so it introduced some risk that we think doesn't offset the (hoped-for!) benefits of reduced flakiness (and maybe slight performance improvements, though that was never a primary driver of the changes).

We talked about whether we should revert all of the changes, or whether we should keep some of them (so long as it's clear how one testing strategy should be used compared to another, to avoid making things harder for future work by devs rather than easier) but I think that it makes sense right now to revert it in its entirety. I'm dipping in and out of test initiatives, amongst my other other work, and I _might_ have proposed trying to keep some of this work if that wasn't the case.. or I might not! We'll still have the changes in the commit history, and the old PR will be available, if we want to pick this up again in the future. It might be useful for when we want to consider lifting-and-shifting some integration tests into "fat unit tests" - we'll see, when (and if) that time arises!

author: ProductiveRage
body:
## What

It seems like quite a lot of flakiness originates from how Redis is involved in our integration tests (citation needed, maybe! 😆). We have some hacks and workarounds to try to isolate tests (key prefixes for Redis stores, to try to segregate data persisted between test classes) but I'm not sure that they are as effective as we would like.

So I wondered about whether we should change the default for integration tests to be to use in-memory stores, in place of Redis stores. Most of the integration tests that hit code paths that involve access to Redis-backed caches aren't explicitly testing the Redis integration, and the tests that _do_ intentionally try to exercise a Redis cache / integration can override the caches used within their own scope such that Redis is called.

Hopefully the changes here achieve greater test isolation, reduce flakiness, and _may_ even make the test suite run faster since cross-process calls to Redis no longer occur!

## How

In crafting this PR, I discovered that the `LocalCache` in the `StackRedis` repo is.. somewhat incomplete. To explore what was missing / not working, I created a wrapper class `LocalCacheWithFixes`. If this PR is merged, we should make these changes to the `StackRedis` repo, and delete the `LocalCacheWithFixes` from the integration tests.

I've made an effort to change only the test code, where possible, and avoid touching the production code - however, a few changes were necessary, such as in the `ChannelSubscription` class, where there was no way to override what caches it would use (and where it _has_ to use a real Redis-back cache because the `ChannelSubscriptionTests` call `SiteActivity.GetForSite(..)` and that relies upon `ExecuteScript` calls to Redis).

## Who

This work is probably best aligned with Scale Pod, and so I'll be asking them whether they think it makes sense to push this PR over the line.

author: dionrhys
body:
`BaseScheduledController` currently has a few `high` severity CodeQL "Uncontrolled format string" alerts:

- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/816
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/815
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/814
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/813
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/812
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/811
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/810
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/security/code-scanning/809

These are alerting because the `IScheduledLog` method implementations on the `BaseScheduledController` are using uncontrolled format strings and are also being treated as valid ASP.NET Core controller actions.

These alerts are valid because ASP.NET Core [does](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/mvc/controllers/actions?view=aspnetcore-9.0#defining-actions) consider these methods to be valid controller actions:

> Public methods on a controller, except those with the `[NonAction]` attribute, are actions.

Here's the CodeQL [source code](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/958d209a8152eaca3bebe0f23a93befa45791a5d/csharp/ql/lib/semmle/code/csharp/frameworks/microsoft/AspNetCore.qll#L225-L231) that flags these methods up as being controller actions:

> ```qll
> /** Gets an action method for this controller. */
> Method getAnActionMethod() {
>   result = this.getAMethod() and
>   result.isPublic() and
>   not result.isStatic() and
>   not result.getAnAttribute() instanceof MicrosoftAspNetCoreMvcNonActionAttribute
> }
> ```

No route attributes are on these methods and no conventional routes are set up on startup to route to these, however it's still best practice to mark any public instance method in a controller as `[NonAction]` when they should never be treated as controller actions.
title: Fix BaseScheduledController CodeQL alerts

author: balpha
body:
We're setting `REGEX_DEFAULT_MATCH_TIMEOUT` on the app domain to set the default timeout for any regular expression that doesn't define their own timeouts.

This value is then read here by the framework:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e0837be345978738d0387055e0eb1e2b989dd787/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/src/System/Text/RegularExpressions/Regex.Timeout.cs#L70

-- and it's only read once, during the static initialization of the `Regex` class. In other words, if we set the app domain data *after* the `Regex` class has ever been referenced, it's already too late.

And at lest in `StackOverflow`, that is unfortunately the case:

https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/51139ef7dafdfd0adefb92afbf86830fd2ce4184/StackOverflow/Startup.cs#L721

That ⬆️ happens way before the [call](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/51139ef7dafdfd0adefb92afbf86830fd2ce4184/StackOverflow/Startup.cs#L911) to `UseStackOverflowCommonAspNet`, where we were setting the app domain data. And thus, Stack Overflow never got the default timeout overridden (which therefore remains infinite, which is the "default default").

It's possible that this still worked in the other projects which use `UseStackOverflowCommonAspNet`, but that feels pretty brittle, so I decided to simply remove the `SetData` call from `UseStackOverflowCommonAspNet` and call it in each individual project's `Program.cs`, as the very first thing.
title: set default regex timeout earlier

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
This PR attempts to resolve an issue where webpack builds would be triggered too often.

The issue here seems to be that when building webpack and the resulting manifest _contents_ do not change, the last modified time of `webpack-manifest.json` isn't updated which on the surface kind of makes sense.

However, this could cause problems when the generated client side product events would have a newer modification time than `webpack-manifest.json` as MSBuild solely checks on file modification times.

As the `webpack-manifest.json` would never be touched, this meant that webpack would always be called on build even if no changes were made to the generated Typescript files.

In this PR we no longer remove `webpack-manifest.json` (which is one approach to solve this) but instead only _touch_ the file to change its modification time. While this is technically the same, it's a bit more robust.

Additionally a problem was identified in the client side product events which triggered this behaviour.

As the original C# class (or `record`) name would be used as the file name for the generated Typescript class this was susceptible to name collisions. And that's exactly what happened, there were naming collisions for:

- QuestionTitleLinkClickEvent
- ModalDismissedEvent
- ModalCompletedEvent

Effectively this meant that the files would be continuously overwritten and therefore receiving a new modification timestamp.

The Roslyn generator has been updated to detect this and raise the `PE0002` diagnostic if it finds a conflict.
title: [DX] Client side product events generation

body:
## Summary
Small change to use interpolation instead of variables for `PostState` and `PostTypeId` in `PostQueryBuilder.cs`. This change allows SQL to more likely make use of filtered indexes potentially improving performance.

Queries without interpolation, note that `PostState` and `PostTypeId` are passed as variables
```
exec sp_executesql N'SELECT P.* , U.* , LastEditorUser.* , PostMetadata.ViewCount
 FROM Posts P /* Helpers\PostQueryBuilder.cs@500 */ 
LEFT JOIN Users U ON U.Id = P.OwnerUserId
LEFT JOIN Users LastEditorUser ON LastEditorUser.Id = P.LastEditorUserId
LEFT JOIN PostMetadata ON PostMetadata.PostId = P.Id
WHERE P.PostTypeId = @PostType AND P.DeletionDate IS NULL AND P.PostState = @State
ORDER BY ISNULL(P.LastActivityDate, P.CreationDate) Desc
OFFSET @start ROWS
FETCH NEXT @size ROWS ONLY
',N'@PostType tinyint,@State tinyint,@start int,@size int',@PostType=1,@State=1,@start=0,@size=30

exec sp_executesql N'SELECT COUNT(*)
 FROM Posts P /* Helpers\PostQueryBuilder.cs@495 */ 
WHERE P.PostTypeId = @PostType AND P.DeletionDate IS NULL AND P.PostState = @State
',N'@PostType tinyint,@State tinyint',@PostType=1,@State=1
```

Queries with interpolation
```
exec sp_executesql N'SELECT P.* , U.* , LastEditorUser.* , PostMetadata.ViewCount
 FROM Posts P /* Helpers\PostQueryBuilder.cs@500 */ 
LEFT JOIN Users U ON U.Id = P.OwnerUserId
LEFT JOIN Users LastEditorUser ON LastEditorUser.Id = P.LastEditorUserId
LEFT JOIN PostMetadata ON PostMetadata.PostId = P.Id
WHERE P.PostTypeId = 1 AND P.DeletionDate IS NULL AND P.PostState = 1
ORDER BY ISNULL(P.LastActivityDate, P.CreationDate) Desc
OFFSET @start ROWS
FETCH NEXT @size ROWS ONLY
',N'@start int,@size int',@start=0,@size=30


SELECT COUNT(*)
 FROM Posts P /* Helpers\PostQueryBuilder.cs@495 */ 
WHERE P.PostTypeId = 1 AND P.DeletionDate IS NULL AND P.PostState = 1
```

## How to Test

1. Run API v3
2. Make an authenticated request to `/questions` with the site setting https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_UseElastic_ForQuestions disabled, it should result in a 200

author: svalbuena
body:
This is a tidy up PR I'm doing before the real changes. We are using InternalsVisibleTo too much, usually this is just done to expose internal methods/classes to the test projects but not to other non-test project.

If project A needs to access an internal property of project B then we need to re-think the design of the internal property of project B like making it public. Using the InternalsVisibleTo makes the code harder to follow, as something you believe is internal in the project can break other projects.

I want to clean this up, and only leave InternalsVisibleTo for unit/integration tests projects, and make the impacted properties public. This should also avoid issues like https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/CBVG8MJQN/p1758562497811019.

I looked at the git history, seems like making internal available for any kind of project was an historical decision to make a .net migration easier, and addressing this "patch" was never done later: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/2869

In this PR i'm consolidating the location of InternalsVisibleTo, at the moment we are mixing using it in .csproj files or in AssemblyInfo.cs files. We should stick with one of the two.
I've usually used .csproj for this, in most cases we can avoid creating the AssemblyInfo.cs file so it's one less file to maintain. It's also more cohesive, since the InternalsVisibleTo is needed when another project references our project, and they do it with ProjectReference directives on their .csproj files.

In a follow up pr i'll remove some of the InternalVisiblesTo directives to try limit this to only testing projects.
title: Consolidate InternalsVisibleTo on .csproj files

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
This PR introduces a new authentication handler specifically for service-to-service calls in the StackOverflow landscape as described in [Simplifying Authentication for Monolith Integration](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iREdZc-DC3R6gASxSQKdnmog6109EMagQXQDTepRthk/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.5zki3rrsw04p).

Depending on configuration, this will allow services using Workload Identity in Kubernetes to authenticate against APIv3 and provides them with the authorization to make _read_ and, when configured via an allow list, _write_ calls.

The way this works is that a service deployed to Kubernetes can request a token via Workload Identity.
That token is then applied in the `Authorization` header on the HTTP request being made to APIv3.

APIv3 is configured to accept tokens from the identity providers in Azure and GCP, which allows it to verify:
- That the issuer is trusted
- That the token signature is valid
- That the requested audience is allowed in

When a token is deemed valid, the handler checks if an `ApiApplication` already exists for the _subject_ (the `sub` claim).
If not, a `ApiApplication` entry is created automatically and linked to the Community User (`accountId` of `-1`). It is also assigned write permissions when the subject identified in the token is on the allow list in the `APIv3_WorkloadIdentity_SubjectsAllowedToWrite` site setting.

The `ApiApplication` is given the type `ApiApplicationType.StackExchange` so we can identify it as one of ours and we can use that information when segregating API call volumes for example for billing purposes.

Subsequent calls will locate the `ApiApplication` by name (the `sub` claim from the token) owned by the community user.

Once these are provided, the `ClaimsIdentity` is constructed similar to the `JwtAccessTokenAuthenticationHandler` or `OpaqueAccessTokenAuthenticationHandler` which in turn is provisioned on the `Current.User`.

## How do we know this works?

Good question!

There are a set of integration tests that verify the behaviour
title: [AUTH] Support Workload Identity authentication for APIv3

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

This implements the banner saying that the user can now comment. It's both implemented in Razor and in svelte, just in case, cause I don't know what UI will be released when we inform users that they can comment.

Why use banner and not for example typical achievements? This way we can inform only part of users => that allows for gradual rollout. It also gives us an option to roll it back if needed (I don't think it's super easy with achievements).

Open question is whether we use a user preference to steer the banner or we create a new table.
- Why user settings? That's the pattern we generally use even for dismissing banners. It also introduces no changes to the db, so it _looks simpler_.
- Why a separate table? Cause we want to have this banner only temporarily. A user setting, if once used, shouldn't be reused, and it's all saved in one column in the db as serialized string. So after we no longer need this setting, some mess still remains. _This is cleaner._

I went with a new table that can be later cleaned up easily.

## How to Test

1. Make sure the [new comments ui is enabled](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.ShowNewFollowUpUIFor)
2. Make sure that [Jones is disabled](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.FollowUpsIndianaJonesEnabledFor)
3. Make sure that [banner is enabled](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.ShowYouCanCommentBannerFor), let's say for one rep users `not Anonymous, not Rep >= 2, All`

author: nhu-van
body:
## Summary

Jira Teams-14752

<ins>**Issues**:</ins>
We updated the daily tag digest scheduler to send every 30 minutes instead of once per day. The scheduled job also sends emails in batches, processing 1000 subscriptions each time. This causes some users to receive multiple emails during a day in the following cases:
- When a user has multiple subscriptions, and their subscriptions are processed in 2 different batches.
- When a user already receives their daily digest email, but they add new watched tags. They will receive another email about the newly added tags at the next scheduled time.

<ins>**To fix the above issues**</ins>:
I updated the subscription query to:
- Group the subscriptions by owners. The batch size will be based on owners instead of individual subscriptions.
- Add `LastProcessedDate` column to indicate that a subscription is picked up by the scheduled route. It may or may not send out an email. 
- Exclude subscriptions if there are subscriptions already processed to the same owner within 24 hours.


## How to Test
- Log in as 3 different users (Example: user1, user2, user3)
- On the home page, add at least **3** watched tags for them. 
- Set watched tags for the first 2 users as "Daily", and the third one as "As soon as possible".
- Add some questions with the above watched tags (Might need to rebuild the Elastic Search to make it work)
- Update the [batch size](https://stackenterprise.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Tags.TagSubscriptionDailyBatchSize) to 1 for testing purposes.
- Run the [daily tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily)
- Check that only 1 email is sent to the **first** user (Ex: user1) and the subscriptions for this user are updated with the last sent date. (Ex: if you have 3 rows in the `TagSetRows` for user1, all 3 rows should be updated) 
```
-- Checking emails
SELECT *
FROM [Local.Enterprise.Sites.Teams].[dbo].[EmailMessages]
ORDER BY CreationDate desc

-- Checking tag subscriptions
SELECT *
FROM [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].dbo.TagSetRows
WHERE TagSetTypeId = 1 AND NotificationFrequencyTypeId = 2 AND OwnerUserId = {YOUR_USER_ID}
```
- Go back the Home page and add a new watched tag for the first user (Ex: user1)
- Run the [daily tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) again
- Check that you only receive 1 email for the **second** user (Ex: user2). The subscription row (`TagSetRows`) of the newly added watched tag should have `NULL` for the `LastSendDate` column. 
- Run the [daily tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) again
- Check that you don't receive any other email
- Run the [15-minute tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-fifteen-minutes)
- Check that you receive 1 email for the **third** user (Ex: user3) and all the subscription rows for this user are updated.
title: Teams-14752-Update tag subscription query to not send new tags within the same day

author: threefjefff
body:
## Summary

When MS Teams starts up, it begins looping through a bunch of write-paths to send chat messages for AutoAnswer. In order to do this, it needs an access token, which is obtained through MSAL. Unfortunately, this can throw exceptions due to poor setup, and due to the fact the Client sets this up, we have no control over throwing a bunch of exceptions in a loop when credentials expire.

In `MicrosoftTeamsApi.GetAuthTokenAsync()` we already have defensive coding around this. AutoAnswer uses a mix of this api and `GraphApiService`, which did not.

This PR adds a `try/catch` for known MSAL exceptions, such that they're propogated to existing exception handling in the AutoAnswer queue
title: Add defensive coding around GraphApi token retrieval paths

## Summary

In @stackoverflow/stacks@v3.0.0-beta.24 we [swapped](https://github.com/StackExchange/Stacks/pull/2172) all references to `--su-static*` sizing custom properties with `--su*` to better support user preferences and accessibility. This means that `--su-static*` were not present anymore in the v3 css bundle we served.

Now, we could have expected the [stacks-v2-scoped file](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/main/StackOverflow/Content/Shared/stacks-v2-scoped.less) to inject those variables for the legacy pages but unfortunately it did not. This is because the `--su-static*` variables are defined in stacks v2 under the `body` selector ([see source code](https://github.com/StackExchange/Stacks/blob/develop/packages/stacks-classic/lib/atomic/spacing.less)) and there is no `body` scoped under our @scope `stacks-v2-start`.

There are though plenty of v2 stacks classes relying on those static variables being exposed which resulted on completely messing up the legacy pages in the beta site. [See thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C097YESGSMB/p1770317888146239)

The solution is to expose those variables again at the scope level (not under the `body` selector) in the stacks-v2-scoped file. This is what this PR does. 

I have tested it locally with a version of the UI composer using the latest stacks.css and things restarted to look good again. Once this PR is merged we can unpin the version of stacks in the UI composer (or at least upgrade the pinned version to the latest).

author: threefjefff
body:
## Overview

Adds support for the `offline_access` grant, which issues a Refresh Token that is redeemable without user intervention to claim an Access Token for up to 30 days after the initial issuance.

This works across all product tiers:
- In Public and Enterprise, the refresh tokens are stored in the Sites DB. They are unadorned at rest and carry a `refresh_` prefix for ease of distinction in transit.
- In FBB, refresh tokens are given channel marks identically to Access Codes. 
    - These encode the channel number and a HMAC in the token such that the outer site can proxy to the correct Channels instance.
    - They are stored in the `Teams.Channels` database, alongside Tokens and Codes.

If an access token is claimed with a client secret, the refresh token must be redeemed with a client secret. The code verification steps for PKCE are intentially a one-shot pass, and cannot be reused in this way, and equally the redemption of refresh tokens is prescribed as a single call.

All refresh tokens are redeemable once. If someone attempts to redeem the refresh token a second time, all refresh tokens associated with the user login session are invalidated, and a new Authorization Code flow will have to be started with user intervention. 

This is in line with [RFC recommendations](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13#section-4.3.1-10.2.1) for issuing refresh tokens to public clients.

## Test

### Public
- Initiate an Auth Code exchange with the `offline_access` scope.
```
https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth
?client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/login_success
&scope=offline_access
&state=lol
&code_challenge=oNH5nU7TKfJhjmQrVd8iUFaafq6fggrTHcZD_FlZILw
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Grab the Code from the response URL
- Exchange the code for a token, ensuring you get a `refresh_token`
```
POST https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmeta.stackexchange.local%2Foauth%2Flogin_success
&code=<CODE_GOES_HERE>
&code_verifier=M5hBOxU0Pxve7ffvo776cANLWqDYuamoltpFfTWZV-RDET8I0akJxxKz7zormRTUelg4bFHMHEETpGJ05Tte8A
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Exchange the refresh token for a token, ensuring you get both a token and refresh token
```
POST https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&refresh_token=<REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE>
&grant_type=refresh_token
```
- Ensure your new access token works, that both the access token and refresh token are different from the original.

### FBB
- Initiate an Auth Code exchange with the `offline_access` scope and the `access_team` scope.
```
https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth
?client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/login_success
&scope=offline_access access_team
&state=lol
&code_challenge=oNH5nU7TKfJhjmQrVd8iUFaafq6fggrTHcZD_FlZILw
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Grab the Code from the response URL
- Exchange the code for a token, ensuring you get a `refresh_token`
```
POST https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/login_success
&code=<CODE_GOES_HERE>
&code_verifier=M5hBOxU0Pxve7ffvo776cANLWqDYuamoltpFfTWZV-RDET8I0akJxxKz7zormRTUelg4bFHMHEETpGJ05Tte8A
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Exchange the refresh token for a token, ensuring you get both a token and refresh token
```
POST https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&refresh_token=<REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE>
&grant_type=refresh_token
```
- Ensure your new access token works for your selected team (but not another team), that both the access token and refresh token are different from the original.

author: threefjefff
body:
## Summary
This is some ground-laying work to make the inclusion of a `grant_type` easier. Functionally, OAuth defines two major endpoints (`Authorization` and `Token`) and prescribes various ways of ushering us through them.:
- `Authorization Code flow` - Well, that's what was already here.
- `Client Credentials flow` - would just be a call to the token endpoint with the right grant type specified
- `Refresh token flow` - is a call to the token endpoint, reidentifying yourself (if required) alongside your refresh token
- even the `Implict` flow was a means of requesting a token response from the `Authorize`  endpoint

Long story short, we've been overcomplicating this for a while, and as we have a need to add a `grant_type` (in order to enable `refresh_token` flow) this is in place to cut down the noise before adding more complexity.

- Renaming the Authorization and Token endpoint handlers to succumb to industry standard nomenclature (we don't even _use_ `implict` flow any more, and `explict` was never the name of the other kind of flow!)
- Simplifying the form data/json endpoints such that they share an implemntation, and hand off interpreting the response to a respective handler.

Tested by unit/integration tests

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
Context in this Slack thread: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C05U5BB3YQN/p1764775578859249?thread_ts=1764770596.818929&cid=C05U5BB3YQN

After a bit of digging to see when the response may have been started before we attempt to set a status code I've found that with web sockets the situation is a little different from regular HTTP calls.
Turns out that when you `await httpContext.WebSockets.AcceptWebSocketAsync()` this sends a `HTTP 101 Switching Protocols` to the client effectively starting the response...
Normally when no problems occur when pumping websocket data back-and-forth the fragment proxy sends a `EmptyResult()` on completion which doesn't touch the `HttpContext.Response` at all.

However, when an exception occurs while we're pumping data we land in a try/catch and return a `ProxyResult.Error` and we drop into the `DevMessageOrErrorPage()` route which _does_ try to change the `HttpContext.Response` and triggers the error we're seeing.
title: [FRAGMENT PROXY] Return empty result when response has already started

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

Yet another special case in how we handle account history:
1. When the user became a developer (thus an employee), we didn't store the related account history - that sometimes happens (still).
2. Then the person left the company and that was stored correctly.
3. Then the person deleted the profile.
4. Then the profile was recreated.
5. If the profile gets recreated shortly after deletion, the createddate is restored from logs. If more time passes, Current.Time is set as creationdate.

So we have a past employee, where we don't have info when this person started the job. I was taking profile creation date as the beginning of the tenure, but that's incorrect in this case... So maybe we should just take min of starting date and the oldest history entry.

Maybe you could even just take the date of the oldest history entry of any type for the related account? That sounds even safer.

## How to Test

There's an integration test added. The edge case is not easy to reproduce locally:
1. Create a user.
7. Make it an employee or a developer through the db, so that no entry occurs. There's also another way to achieve that through our API, but I'm not sure how. Editing account type correctly stores the account history, so that's not helpful in this case.
8. Ask a question.
9. Edit the account type to Registered.
10. Delete the user.
11. Modify the traces in log to delete "creationdate" from log entry.
12. Undelete the user.
13. Go to the created question and see the badge (or don't, if it's fixed already).

Alternatively you could clear the log entries and recreate the user, but I'm not sure how to do that locally.
title: fix a weird edge case in calculating employee tenures

## Summary

- Folds the standalone `.github/workflows/trigger-analysis.yaml` workflow into the tail of the `build` job in `build_test_package.yml`, then deletes the original file.
- Preserves the `**.cs` / `**.cshtml` / `**.razor` path filtering by comparing changed files via `gh api repos/.../compare/<before>...<sha>` instead of GitHub's workflow-level `paths:` trigger.
- Dispatch is gated to `matrix.configuration == 'Release' && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` so it fires once per push to main, matching the original scope.

## Behavior change worth flagging

The analysis trigger previously fired regardless of whether the main build succeeded — it was its own workflow listening for the same push. After this change it only fires if the `Release` matrix entry of the `build` job succeeds. Reasonable trade-off (no point analyzing a broken build), but flagging in case anyone was relying on the old behavior.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on this PR: confirm the two new steps appear in the `build` job and are **skipped** on every matrix entry (PR runs are excluded by the `if:` condition).
- [ ] After merge to `main`: confirm the steps run on the `Release` matrix entry and skip on the other three. If the merge touched a `.cs`/`.cshtml`/`.razor` file, confirm a workflow run shows up at https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.Analyzers/actions/workflows/analyze-stackoverflow.yml for the merge SHA.
- [ ] Sanity-check a docs-only commit on main afterwards — the trigger step should be skipped (output `trigger=false`).

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

This PR looks at the integration tests we have for votes and restructures them.

### What's the goal

The goal is to have a living doc of all requirements. Ultimately, having a reasonably full and readable test coverage/living doc will enable us to use claude more efficiently. Much less stress about introducing regression errors cause the critical functionality is covered, and if something break, we exactly know what.

### Why the naming

Each test should describe what requirement(s) it tests and what functionality is broken when the test is red. Naming connected to requirements allows us for faster assessment of the criticality of the bug. Grouping by functionality rather than for class tested allows us to easier look for related problems and edge cases.

### Why integration tests

The first reason is that those tests are overarching the db, modules and the monolith code, so they can be very helpful when we decide to modularize stuff with Claude's help.
The other reason is that they are easier to connect to requirements than unit tests - smaller chance that claude gets it wrong.
Is it ideal? No. Is it fast and robust to errors? I think so.

### What's included

I focused on the voting and all of its types. The tests themselves were not changed. No new tests were introduced. I only moved the tests around, regrouped them and made sure that the names make sense.

### Tradeoffs

The naming was generated by Claude. It may be wrong. But, when reviewing the test names and comparing them to the old ones, I often caught myself realizing why a test was introduced in the first place. That's a huge win for me. If you agree and also find this helpful, let's merge it and I'll move on to a next domain.
title: Refactor votes tests

author: dc9842
body:
## Summary

Fixes the ask page prefill flow used by trusted services (e.g., SKI claim links) so that prefilled draft data and correlation IDs survive model translation into the V3 ask experience.

### 1. Refactor AskPrefillHmacVerifier

Addresses review feedback from #25129:

- `VerifySignature` now returns `AskPrefillVerifyResult` enum with specific failure reasons instead of `bool`
- New `ResolveServiceKey` method separates key lookup from HMAC verification

No behavior change — the controller still returns 400 for all verification failures.

### 2. Carry prefilled draft through V3 ask page model

`AskViewAsync` translates from `AskModel` to `V3.AskModel` without carrying the `QuestionDraft` through. The V3 model lazily loads from the DB draft store, losing the HMAC-signed prefill data. This caused prefilled fields to render empty on the V3 ask page.

Fix: detect `PrefilledAskModel` in `AskViewAsync` and copy `Draft` + `AdditionalEventArgs` to the V3 model.

### 3. Carry correlation_id through V3 ask view

The V3 view generates a random `Guid` for `CorrelationId`, discarding the trusted-service `correlation_id` (e.g., `"ski:{token}"`) needed for the `question.asked` → AEH → `mark_posted` flow.

Fix: read `correlation_id` from `AdditionalEventArgs` with Guid fallback.

### 4. Pass AdditionalEventArgs through the V3 Svelte island

The V3 island submits `CorrelationId` as a top-level form field, but the `question.asked` product event reads from `AdditionalArgs` (populated by `add-*` prefixed form fields scanned by `ExtractInsertFromForm`). The V1 ask page handles this by rendering `AdditionalEventArgs` as hidden `<input name="add-{key}">` elements — V3 had no equivalent.

Fix: pass `AdditionalEventArgs` from the cshtml through the island args → Svelte context → `SubmitControls`, which appends each entry as `add-{key}` in the `FormData`. This ensures the `question.asked` event receives the correlation_id on both V1 and V3 paths.

### Prefill flow end-to-end

1. Trusted service generates a draft and signs `(service, title, body, tags, correlation_id)` with HMAC-SHA256
2. User visits claim link → auto-POST form to `/questions/ask/prefill` (unauthenticated users go through login redirect via `SessionState` and restore at `/questions/ask/prefill/restore`)
3. SO verifies HMAC → renders prefilled ask page with draft data and `AdditionalEventArgs`
4. User submits → `question.asked` event fires to AEH with the trusted-service `CorrelationId`
5. Downstream listener matches the correlation_id prefix and marks the draft as posted

Steps 3 and 4 were broken on V3: step 3 because the draft was lost in model translation, and step 4 because the correlation_id was replaced by a random Guid (view) and never submitted as an `add-*` field (island).

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `AskPrefillVerifyResult.cs` | New 7-value result enum |
| `AskPrefillHmacVerifier.cs` | `ResolveServiceKey` + two `VerifySignature` overloads |
| `QuestionsController.Ask.cs` | Enum comparison + carry `Draft`/`AdditionalEventArgs` to V3 model |
| `V3/Ask.Model.cs` | Add `set` accessor to `Draft` property |
| `V3/Ask.cshtml` | Read `correlation_id` from `AdditionalEventArgs`; pass `AdditionalEventArgs` to island |
| `index.mod.ts` | Map `AdditionalEventArgs` to island props |
| `types.ts` | Add `additionalEventArgs` to `AskQuestionProps` and `SubmitFormData` |
| `AskQuestion.svelte` | Thread `additionalEventArgs` through Svelte context |
| `SubmitControls.svelte` | Append `add-{key}` form fields from `additionalEventArgs` |
| `SubmitControls.test.ts` | 3 new tests for `add-*` field submission |
| `AskPrefillHmacVerifierTest.cs` | Assert specific enum values + new tests (30 total) |

- [x] All 9 `SubmitControls` tests pass (6 existing + 3 new)

author: dc9842
body:
## Summary

Adds a generic, HMAC-signed prefill endpoint to the ask page. Trusted services (initially SKI — Stack Knowledge Intelligence) sign draft question fields with HMAC-SHA256 and POST-redirect users to the SO monolith, which verifies the signature and renders a prefilled ask page.

The design is **generic and reusable** — a `service` identifier selects the HMAC key from a JSON map (`AskPagePrefillHMACKeys`), so future services can prefill the ask page without monolith changes.

We use a POST form redirect (auto-submitting hidden form) rather than a GET redirect with query parameters because question bodies routinely exceed browser URL length limits (~2,000 characters).

## HMAC signature scheme

```
String-to-sign: {service}\n{title}\n{body}\n{tags}\n{correlation_id}
Key lookup:     AskPagePrefillHMACKeys[service]  (JSON map → base64-encoded key)
```

The `service` field is included in the signature to prevent cross-service forgery. The `correlation_id` is opaque to the monolith — just passed through to the `question.asked` Event Hub event.

**Browser CRLF normalization:** Browsers convert `\n` to `\r\n` in form values during POST submission (per HTML spec). The verifier canonicalizes `\r\n` → `\n` before computing the HMAC so signatures match regardless of transport.

## How it works

```
Calling service (e.g. SKI)           SO monolith
──────────────────────────           ───────────
GET /claim/{token}
  ├─ sign_draft(service="ski", title,
  │  body, tags, correlation_id, key)
  └─ render auto-submit POST form
       │
       ▼
                              POST /questions/ask/prefill
                                ├─ AskPrefillHmacVerifier.VerifySignature(service, ...)
                                ├─ Key lookup: AskPagePrefillHMACKeys[service]
                                ├─ if authenticated → PrefilledAskPageAsync()
                                └─ if not → PendingFormPush + redirect to login
                                              │
                                              ▼
                                     GET /questions/ask/prefill/restore
                                       └─ PendingFormPop → PrefilledAskPageAsync()
                                              │
                                              ▼
                                     User submits question
                                       └─ QuestionSubmitEvent.CorrelationId = correlation_id
                                            → Event Hub → calling service tracks conversion
```

## Tasks
- **Task 1**: `AskPagePrefillHMACKeys` site setting (JSON map of service→key) + `AskPrefillHmacVerifier` static helper using `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`
- **Task 2**: `POST /questions/ask/prefill` (XSRF-exempt, HMAC-protected) and `GET /questions/ask/prefill/restore` endpoints on `QuestionsController` with `PendingFormPush`/`Pop` for unauthenticated users
- **Task 3**: Nullable `CorrelationId` on `QuestionSubmitEvent` so the `question.asked` Event Hub event includes the draft claim token

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `SiteSettings.AskPage.cs` | Added `AskPagePrefillHMACKeys` with `[Secret]` — JSON map of service name → base64 key |
| `AskPrefillHmacVerifier.cs` | **New.** Generic HMAC-SHA256 verifier: looks up service key from JSON, CRLF canonicalization, constant-time comparison |
| `DataKeys.cs` | Added `FormTypeKeys.AskPrefill` |
| `QuestionsController.Ask.cs` | Added `AskPrefill` (XSRF-exempt, `service` param), `AskPrefillRestore`, `RenderPrefilledAskPageAsync` |
| `QuestionEvents.cs` | Added nullable `CorrelationId` to `QuestionSubmitEvent` + `CreateEvent` |
| `EventRecording.QandA.cs` | Extracts `prefill_correlation_id` from `AdditionalArgs`, passes to event |
| `AskPrefillHmacVerifierTest.cs` | **New.** 16 tests (valid, tampered fields, CRLF normalization, service isolation, multi-service keys, unknown service, null/invalid JSON) |

## Bugs found and fixed during E2E testing

| Bug | Root Cause | Fix |
|-----|-----------|------|
| Browser POST returned "Suspicious request" (fkey missing) | SO's anti-CSRF check rejects cross-origin POSTs | Added `EnsureXSRFSafe = false` — endpoint is protected by HMAC instead |
| Browser POST returned 400 (HMAC mismatch) | Browsers normalize `\n` → `\r\n` in form values per HTML spec | Added `\r\n` → `\n` canonicalization in `AskPrefillHmacVerifier` before verification |

## E2E test results

Tested against SO PR environment (`25129.stackoverflow.cloud`) and SKI dev gateway (`api.ascn-dev.stackoverflow.dev`).

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Claim page renders auto-submitting POST form with all fields | **PASS** |
| Missing draft → 404 | **PASS** |
| Invalid/tampered HMAC → 400 | **PASS** |
| Valid HMAC + unauthenticated → login redirect with PendingFormPush | **PASS** |
| Valid HMAC + authenticated → prefilled ask page (title, body, tags) | **PASS** |

## Test plan

- [x] `AskPrefillHmacVerifierTest` — 16 tests pass
- [x] Solution builds clean (`dotnet build -c Debug`)
- [x] Provision `AskPagePrefillHMACKeys` in dev site settings
- [x] E2E: SKI gateway claim link → auto-submit form → prefilled ask page with correct title/body/tags
- [x] E2E: Unauthenticated flow → login redirect → prefilled ask page
- [x] E2E: Invalid/tampered HMAC → 400
- [ ] E2E: `AskPagePrefillHMACKeys` not configured → 404
- [ ] E2E: Submit prefilled question → verify `question.asked` event has `CorrelationId`

## Deployment notes

- **No new NuGet packages** — uses built-in `System.Security.Cryptography` and `System.Text.Json`
- **Feature-gated**: returns 404 when `AskPagePrefillHMACKeys` is empty (safe to deploy before key provisioning)
- **XSRF-exempt**: prefill endpoint skips fkey validation since it's authenticated via HMAC (same pattern as `/oauth/access_token`)
- **Backwards compatible**: `CorrelationId` is nullable, null for all non-prefill questions
- **Multi-service ready**: add a new service by adding a key to the JSON map — no code changes needed
- SKI gateway side can be deployed independently; E2E testing requires both sides deployed with matching HMAC key

## References

- Proposal: [027-prefilled-ask-page-via-so-module.md](https://github.com/StackEng/ml-stack-knowledge-intelligence/blob/feat/027-prefilled-ask/docs/proposals/027-prefilled-ask-page-via-so-module.md)

## Summary

*New endpoints to handle user clicking on Show Classic or Beta link in the old and new sites.*

Note: This the first of three PRs. These endpoints need to exist before we merge the next PR. The last PR will make use of these cookies/preferences. 

There is a button on the beta site to "Switch to Classic." This takes a user from the beta site to the old site. There is also a button on the old site to "Try new [beta] Site" which takes a user from the old site to the beta site. 
Updating these links to point to one of two new endpoints in the monolith first, followed by a redirect to either the beta site or the old site. Depending on the user type, the endpoint will first do one of the following two things::
* Anonymous users: add a value to the anonymous cookie saying marking if the user prefers the beta or old site
* Authenticated user: add a new value to the `PreferencesRaw` column in the User table stating if the user prefers the beta or old site

The cookie/preference will be used later ([another PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24989)) when we start directing a subset of traffic from the old site to the new site. If the preference or cookie states that a user prefers the old/classic site, then we will ignore if they are part of the subset of users (via the PeopleSelector) that gets redirect from the old site to the beta site.

## How to Test (anonymous user)

1. As an anonymous user, you may have a cookie like `localusr`  This will not initially have a value for Preference `228` in the string
2. Go to the old site
3. Click on "try new [beta] site"
4. You will be first directed to an endpoint on the old site that sets the anon cookie to include `228:true`
5. You will then be forwarded from the exact same page you are on in the monolith (i.e. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/php) to the equivalent page in the beta site (i.e. https://beta.stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/php)
6. Click on the "Switch to classic" button
7. The anon cookie will now have `228:false`

2. Go to the old site
3. Click on "try new [beta] site"
4. You will be first directed to an endpoint on the old site that sets the Preference value in the User table to include `228:true`
5. You will then be forwarded from the exact same page you are on in the monolith (i.e. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/php) to the equivalent page in the beta site (i.e. https://beta.stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/php)
6. Click on the "Switch to classic" button
7. The preferences will now have `228:false`
8. You will end up on the same page on the monolith

This PR upgrades `System.Data.SqlClient` to `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`.

This comes down to:
- Changing all the package references from `System.Data.SqlClient` to `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`.
- Updating all connection strings to have `TrustServerCertificate=true`. This is a [breaking change](https://github.com/dotnet/SqlClient/blob/main/porting-cheat-sheet.md#functionality-changes) where the default value changed from true to false and since we don't have trusted certificates in production we now need this.
- Update dependencies for `StackMail`, `TagEngine`, `StackExchange.Events`, `StackExchange.Exceptional`, `AdServer.Sdk` , `StackExchange.SqlMigrator` and `StackExchange.Compliance` and some framework packages that had a transitive dependency on System.Data.SqlClient.
- Update the reflection code for the SQL timers to use the new namespaces

I deployed this PR all the way to main-prod and let it run for over an hour. I also ran various heavy scheduled routes. I found no issues.
